findings.claim: sfcp-q33 is recall-level for a graded item. Its controller block, ItemController with @ExceptionHandler(ItemNotFound.class), @ResponseStatus(NOT_FOUND) and an Err body, is the porting page's explanation snippet verbatim. The key restates the page's next sentence ('A non-numeric id fails path-variable conversion with MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException, which a 400 handler catches'), and the /items/99 and /items/abc setup is the formative 'o2 400 or 404' item. The standard applied in this loop is the one behind sfcp-sme-01 and the new-15 q35 medium. An item is medium only when remembering an answered question (a bank item, or a page predict/apply question) gives the key with no further step. Reusing an explanatory example's surface is low. q33 meets only the low form: the formative item decides the status pairing, not the handler, and option B (moving the handler into advice) still needs a reasoning step. The key is correct and unique (executed earlier on JDK 25 / Boot 4.1.2, sme-findings-new15.json). q31, which reuses the rest-controllers curl example for case (a), was judged under the same standard as acceptable: cases (b) and (c) need two further applications of the page rules.
findings.recommendation: Optional: re-skin q33 away from the page snippet (another resource and error record), and add the taught twist 'Handlers in a controller cover only that controller', for example by putting an existing MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException handler in a different controller as one distractor's premise, so that the key needs one more step than recall.

findings.claim: Cross-item leak from new q33 into base q01. q33's stem shows the ported controller with @PathVariable long id and states that 'GET /items/abc' answers '400 {"timestamp":...,"status":400,"error":"Bad Request",...}'. In other words, a non-numeric path variable is rejected with Boot's default 400 before the method runs. That is exactly the deciding fact of case (c) in q01 (line 4: @PathVariable long id, request /payments/abc/refunds). It refutes q01 option B, '(a) and (c), with id set to 0 in (c)', outright, so q01 drops to three live options for any learner who has seen q33. The blueprint sets no sequential navigation and the bank does not fix item order. This is the same pattern the Spring loop-3 critics rated medium in CFE-22 (a stem stating a conversion or binding outcome that refutes another item's distractor). The new-15 SME critic noted the overlap but judged it not material without a stated standard; this loop applies the CFE-22 standard. The q01 and q33 keys themselves are correct and unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Remove the shared fact from one of the two items. Simplest: change q33's failing case so its stem does not show a path-variable conversion failure. For example, make the missing piece the 404 side (a ported route whose ItemNotFound handler sits in another controller, using the taught rule 'Handlers in a controller cover only that controller'), or a required @RequestParam that is not part of q01. Re-execute the key. Alternatively, deliver the checkpoint with sequential navigation (no going back) and record that in the blueprint instructions and evidence. Re-run the cross-item scan on the changed bytes.
